title: Custos conformance vector ledger
revision: v2, 2026-08-07 — re-anchored to the ratified Custos 4.2
note: The corpus, not the harness. Each entry states an input shape and the expected result, at the grade the ratified law can currently carry. A disagreement about an expected value is a finding against the specification, never a bug report against an engine. Re-anchored to the ratified 4.2 edition on 2026-08-07; entries assigned by a ruling keep that ruling as their authority and carry the ratified site where the ruled text now lives.

grade_discipline.rule: R5, as clarified by supplement 1 C-1
grade_discipline.statement: Until the carriage encoding ratifies, every expected value here is semantic-grade: the full payload of the conformance predicate (finding value; self-convicted kind; grounds in canonical order; typed requirement set including species; refusal grounds with the seal kind named per section 9's three-kind discipline; cited law head; corpus identity, which carries the admission set). A same-engine comparison may run byte-grade under a pinned fixture-local serialization. A divergence report states its grade.

sources.note: the edition of record, ratified 2026-08-06, anchored at KEL sn 191/192
the predecessor; entries derived from it keep their predecessor site recorded
errata against the ratified edition; both bind as reading rules now

families.order: Permuted arrival and every other presentation-order question. Ratified section 17.
families.equivalence: One governance act expressed two lawful ways, folding to one result.
families.boundary: Must-reject. The exhibit that a wall can actually refuse.
families.refusal: The pending/refusal line, drawn at the grain the law draws it.
families.recognition: Enacted reservation as committed evidence, against external recognition no vector may presume.
families.ordering: Canonical order and the keys it ranges over.
families.transition: Edges of the section 7.3 system, permitted and forbidden.
families.conviction: Bearing, duplicity, antinomy, and what convicts whom.
families.membership: Which spans are the GEL, and what happens when that is underivable.
families.disclosure: Blinding, clause membership, and presentation form.
families.availability: Witness state, receipts, and what the charter binds.
families.observation: Typed evidence about observed key state.
families.compact-form: Section 19's compact receipt form and the three gates that stand it up.

vectors.input: One governance stream presented in several permuted arrival orders, each permutation a distinct presentation of the same committed spans.
vectors.expect: Every permutation folds to the same Constitution. A fold result that varies with arrival order, storage order or any ambient sequence does not conform.

vectors.input: One governance act expressed under each of the two lawful event-form tracks.
vectors.expect: Both fold to the same result. This vector is held to the extent R19 may collapse the tracks; it is written so it stays valid under either outcome.

vectors.input: A governance event whose identity is not self-addressing.
vectors.expect: Must-reject.

vectors.input: An act of a designated class - charter, revocation of a seat, enactment amending law, or a succession act - anchored in an interaction event rather than an establishment event.
vectors.expect: Must-reject. Section 9's anchor-grade rule makes the designated classes establishment-anchored.

vectors.input: A stream placing governance events under both tracks with no committed placement law.
vectors.expect: Must-reject.

vectors.input: A stream whose initial track, or whose ilk table, cannot be derived from the applicable founding-law referent.
vectors.expect: Must-reject. Under R15 this is the same refusal as an underivable GEL membership: designation and membership fail loud or not at all.

vectors.input: A grammar migration not admitted under the grammar previously in force.
vectors.expect: Must-reject.

vectors.input: Compact-form use while any of its ordered gates remains unstood.
vectors.expect: Must-reject.

vectors.input: A pair: an unrecognized governance ilk under a derivable grammar, against an ilk whose grammar itself cannot be derived.
vectors.expect: The first yields committed evidence and a rule-governed judgment. The second fires refusal. The line is drawn at the grammar grain, not at the ilk.

vectors.input: A genus reservation enacted in the GEL and consumed as committed evidence.
vectors.expect: The enactment and its consumption are derivable. External recognition is not presumed by any vector, and under S3-8 the stewardship surface is stated rather than assumed.

vectors.input: A question affirmed at one position, after which the grounding credential's registry emits a revocation event, and the question is asked again at a later position.
vectors.expect: Two independent findings at two coordinates. The affirmed at its position stands; the later position returns what full discharge over the grown bundle yields. No edge of the transition table is crossed, because nothing mutates.

vectors.input: A bundle that discharges enough of the committed requirement space to exhibit one defeat, while another enumerated check remains unexamined.
vectors.expect: Pending, carrying the unexamined check as its typed requirement. Not defeated. An engine that returns the first defeat it finds fails this vector.

vectors.input: The executed divergence from finding #27: one committed input over which two blind engines emitted different pending findings, because their requirement-set dedup keys omitted species.
vectors.expect: The ruled reading. Species is the fourth field of both the dedup key and the canonical order, so two elements agreeing at subject, kind and citing clauses but differing in species are two elements and both survive deduplication.

vectors.input: Two defeats simultaneously available for one question, agreeing in defeater-class rank and citation identifier, differing only in subcode, where one subcode is empty.
vectors.expect: The defeat with a subcode is cited. Presence is the primary key of the subcode component, so the empty subcode orders last rather than first. This is the vector the 4.1 gauntlet and census both missed.

vectors.input: Two requirement sets differing only in the internal order of one element's citing-clause list, and a second pair whose citing-clause lists are of unequal length with the shorter a prefix of the longer.
vectors.expect: Identical serialized sets for the first pair, since the list is ordered before it is used as a sort component. For the second, the shorter list compares less.

vectors.input: A question affirmed above, after which a lower tier self-convicts and the conviction enters the record as new committed spans.
vectors.expect: At the next position, pending, carrying the taint as a typed requirement element of species unresolved-conflict. No fifth codomain value appears. The affirmed stands at its own coordinate.

vectors.input: A self-addressing SAID pin whose placeholder differs in length from the digest it stands in for, and an external whole-file digest pin computed over bytes stripped of the published header.
vectors.expect: Both must-reject. The placeholder is same-length in the digest's own field; the external pin's preimage is the file as published.

vectors.input: Two competing versions of one event at one coordinate, both entering the evidence bundle.
vectors.expect: Duplicity conviction. The fold makes no selection between them, and no vector may present the pair as an input to a choice. Survival is settled below the fold, at bundle assembly, by the medium's own policy.

vectors.input: Three grounded derivations that are pairwise consistent and jointly unsatisfiable, with the joint-unsatisfiability exhibit and the enactment signatures of every producing clause.
vectors.expect: Self-convicted, with a circuit payload carrying the whole set. An engine built to a pair-shaped payload either fails to convict or convicts on an arbitrary two of the three and misstates the ground. This is the discriminating record between circuit-payload and pair-payload engines.

vectors.input: An invocation at an uncommitted composition seam, replayed by two verifiers holding the same committed triple.
vectors.expect: Both refuse, and the refusal is derivable from the triple rather than read off a record. The vector asserts determinism over the decision and asserts nothing about a committed refusal-record form, which section 15's second openness question leaves open.

vectors.input: A conviction-grade pair at the registry or governance tier, within a frame that committed the violated predicate, where the convicted party's artifact is cited in the finding's evidence bundle.
vectors.expect: Bearing holds: conviction and pertinence both. Subject-pertinence fires the edge into self-convicted.

vectors.input: A conviction-grade pair whose convicted party's artifact appears nowhere in the finding's birth-committed declaration.
vectors.expect: No bearing. Pertinence fails, so no edge fires, and the finding stands as computed.

vectors.input: A bearing-shaped pair inside a frame that never committed the violated predicate.
vectors.expect: Consumption, not refusal and not conviction. No committed predicate means no conviction, so the pair is ordinary evidence. Axiom 3's refusal guards law running out on the question, never on this gate.

vectors.input: An antinomy circuit one of whose producing clauses is a member of the finding's discharged requirement space.
vectors.expect: Bearing by the clause-membership branch of pertinence. Flat membership in a finite committed enumeration decides it; no transitive closure is walked.

vectors.input: A conviction of a cited third party rather than of the question's own subject.
vectors.expect: Ground-pertinence, which fires R6's taint succession - pending, species unresolved-conflict - and not the edge into self-convicted. The finding's voice is poisoned; the question is not.

vectors.input: A defeated finding whose cited defeat is later falsified by committed evidence undercutting the defeater's own enactment.
vectors.expect: An ordinary succession at a new position, computed fresh by full discharge, possibly affirmed. The prior defeated stands at its coordinate. Reinstatement is a new fact, never an edge.

vectors.input: A defeated finding against which added evidence supplies contrary weight without falsifying any ground the finding cites.
vectors.expect: No reversal. The reversal condition admits undercut and not rebuttal.

vectors.input: A falsifier that strikes an artifact absent from the prior finding's cited ground.
vectors.expect: No reversal. The reversal condition is computed through R13's pertinence, so an artifact outside the birth-committed declaration cannot undercut.

vectors.input: The eloquent stranger: a well-formed warranty citing a law head folded from a registry the subject's founding law never designated.
vectors.expect: Must-reject. The law head SHALL be derivable through the designation chain, and recognition weight does not substitute for designation.

vectors.input: The two-team pair: one committed record from which two independent implementations would each derive a different GEL span set under their own membership conventions.
vectors.expect: Refusal, and not either invention. The vector's expected value is the refusal itself, which is what makes it discriminating.

vectors.input: A stream whose governance registry cannot be derived from committed bytes.
vectors.expect: The bootstrap refusal, extended from placement to membership. Any membership rule that can yield a proper subset of the GEL without a refusal is must-reject.

vectors.input: A covenant seal naming a clause set, and a successor whose satisfaction of that set is asked as a standing question.
vectors.expect: A four-valued finding, position-indexed, inheriting bearing, reinstatement, designated law and full discharge. Satisfaction is a fold, not a byte comparison and not a negotiation.

vectors.input: A covenant seal placed over content for which byte equality is achievable and a digest seal is therefore mandatory.
vectors.expect: Must-reject. Where byte equality is achievable the digest seal is mandatory, and a covenant seal over digest-sealable content is the defect.

vectors.input: A covenant seal whose satisfaction finding comes back defeated.
vectors.expect: Breach with a committed anchor. The seal carries the question and the fold supplies the answer; the composition of the two is what makes breach computable.

vectors.input: An object whose SAID is committed in advance of intended disclosure, carrying no blinding factor.
vectors.expect: Must-reject. The blinding factor is substrate-grade, in ACDC's u-field discipline.

vectors.input: A born-disclosed object whose SAID is committed with no blinding factor.
vectors.expect: Admitted. Born-disclosed objects are exempt, and a vector that rejects them would over-apply the mandate.

vectors.input: A replay whose engine holds a revision of a consumed external specification differing from the revision the Constitution commits.
vectors.expect: Refusal, fail-loud. A semantics-pin mismatch is not a silent divergence, and a divergence report over unequal pins says so rather than reporting nonconformance.

vectors.input: A pinned rule that the Constitution's prose never mentions but that the pinned revision nonetheless governs.
vectors.expect: It governs. The enumeration clause is a functional-dependency declaration over the predicate set consumed, so completeness of the prose is not what makes a pinned rule binding.

vectors.input: A three-slot compound invocation in which two components compute findings and the third refuses.
vectors.expect: The invocation refuses, with grounds named per section 9's three-kind discipline, and the refusal record cites both computed components, which stand as ordinary findings at their own coordinates. No product object contains a refused coordinate.

vectors.input: An ACDC edge slot fed to a signing-threshold evaluator with no standing appraisal of the referenced credential - no schema check, no issuer qualification, no registry state, no disclosure state.
vectors.expect: Must-diverge from the ruled reading. The weighted-threshold satisfaction shape is shared; the slot judgment is this document's fold question and does not transfer from the substrate.

vectors.input: A revealed clause with its blinding factor, presented against the anchored aggregate commitment over the Constitution's per-clause sub-blocks.
vectors.expect: Must-affirm membership. The verifier recomputes the clause's membership in the aggregate without seeing its siblings, which remain provably present and unreadable.
vectors.ratified_site: not carried — S3-3 structure ruled, carriage to the encoding round

vectors.input: A forged sibling sub-block offered as a member of the anchored aggregate.
vectors.expect: Must-refuse.
vectors.ratified_site: not carried — S3-3 structure ruled, carriage to the encoding round

vectors.input: One finding presented three ways: replay presentation disclosing the evidence blocks; warranted presentation citing finding, clause, evidence commitment and lens; proof presentation bound to the same commitments.
vectors.expect: The three are discriminated rather than conflated. Proving a clause's membership is not proving satisfaction of hidden evidence, and a vector that treats the three as interchangeable reproduces the defect this ruling repairs.
vectors.ratified_site: not carried — S3-3 structure ruled, carriage to the encoding round

vectors.input: A warranty whose edge to its warrantor's seat credential carries the DI2I operator, where the warrantor holds no such seat.
vectors.expect: Must-fail credential verification, before any fold runs. The check is evidence the fold consumes, never a verdict, so the two currents stay unmerged.
vectors.ratified_site: not carried — S3-4 seat-credential edge discipline, successor obligation

vectors.input: An establishment event whose new witness state falls below the floor its stratum's availability charter commits.
vectors.expect: Must-convict from the KEL bytes alone, derivable by any holder. Witness configuration is a governed object class.
vectors.ratified_site: not carried — S3-5 charter binding, successor obligation

vectors.input: A verification cone root whose receipt threshold is unsatisfied, with some receipt indices missing.
vectors.expect: Pending, whose typed requirement set enumerates the missing receipt indices. The cone root carries a typed authentication grade: controller threshold verified, witness roster identified, receipt threshold satisfied, establishment coordinate cited.
vectors.ratified_site: not carried — S3-5 authentication grade, successor obligation

vectors.input: A schema-typed watcher discrepancy report offered as evidence in a bundle.
vectors.expect: Admissible in E as committed evidence. A judge's or juror's determination over it is replayable evidence and never a fold replacement.
vectors.ratified_site: not carried — S3-7 typed observation evidence, successor obligation

vectors.input: A schema-typed key-state-notice comparison package offered as evidence in a bundle.
vectors.expect: Admissible in E as committed evidence. The acquisition procedure that produced it is expressly open, and no vector may presume one.
vectors.ratified_site: not carried — S3-7 typed observation evidence, successor obligation

vectors.input: The interregnum triple, the stale-quorum rotation, the covenant-violating ordinary rotation, and the covenant-conforming recovery.
vectors.expect: Held with their items. These families cannot be specified until the owed ruling lands on the recovery-branch exception grammar, because a covenant must not convict the medium's lawful cure and the exception must itself be committed law.
vectors.held_on: the recovery-seam ruling owed by S3-9, awaiting supplement 4

vectors.ratified_site: §8.3 required payloads, L1659-1660, read under E4-1
vectors.input: A self-convicted finding whose kind is duplicity, carrying the canonical proof package for the contradictory pair.
vectors.expect: Must-affirm. The payload obligation is discharged by the package that matches the conviction's kind, and the pair is the right package for this kind.

vectors.ratified_site: §8.3 required payloads, L1659-1660, against §8.4 L1824-1832, read under E4-1
vectors.input: A self-convicted finding whose kind is antinomy, carrying a jointly-unsatisfiable circuit of cardinality three where no two derivations contradict.
vectors.expect: Must-affirm. This vector discriminates against a pair-only reading of the payload bullet: an engine that rejects a circuit-shaped payload because the bullet says 'the contradictory pair' fails here, and the erratum says the pair wording confers no such licence.

vectors.ratified_site: §8.3 canonical selection, L1766-1779, read under E4-2
vectors.input: One defeat available for a question, carrying an empty subcode, and no other defeat at that (defeater-class rank, citation identifier).
vectors.expect: Must-select it. 'Orders last' is a tie-break annotation, so an absent subcode compares greater only against a present subcode at the same rank and identifier, and has no other effect. An engine reading 'orders last' as a global sort key demotes the only available defeat below tuples that do not exist and fails here.

vectors.input: A membership rule that yields a proper subset of the GEL without firing a refusal.
vectors.expect: Must-reject. Designation and membership fail loud or not at all; a silently shorter GEL is the poison R15 records under partial disclosure.

vectors.input: One warranted receipt bundle presented in both presentation orders.
vectors.expect: Identical bundle identifier and identical fold consequence. This is the equivalence family of gate three.

vectors.input: A receipt bundle tampered in one byte, in any group.
vectors.expect: Must-reject.

vectors.input: A forged group identity, offered with a between-group permutation.
vectors.expect: Must-reject. Canonical reassembly does not cure a forged group identity, and a vector that lets reassembly cure it is testing the wrong thing.

vectors.input: The bundle identifier offered where the receipted event's identifier is required, and the converse.
vectors.expect: A conforming consumer SHALL refuse the confusion in both directions. The two digests are different types.

vectors.input: An unseated ilk in the compact form.
vectors.expect: Must-reject.

vectors.input: A compact-form stream whose routes are not isolated as gate three requires.
vectors.expect: Must-reject. Route isolation is a member of the must-reject family in its own right.

vectors.input: A warranted heavyweight envelope fed to an ungoverned KERI node at the pinned checkout.
vectors.expect: The receipt MUST verify and the stream MUST survive the extra attachment groups. This is the vanilla-passthrough family, at gate grade: an envelope grouping that fails is redesigned until it passes, because compatibility is a gate rather than a hope.
